text: Synthesizing Arrow's impossibility theorem, the Folk Theorems, and incomplete-contract theory implies that any fixed governance rule set is eventually dominated, so durable cooperation requires architecture that governs its own evolution.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, From Neoclassical to Computative Labor: Foundations for a Testable Theory of Reputation Governance in the Agent Economy (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6890879

isBasedOn.name: From Neoclassical to Computative Labor: Foundations for a Testable Theory of Reputation Governance in the Agent Economy

abstract: Read together, these results imply that any fixed governance rule set is eventually dominated, and that durable cooperation therefore requires architecture that governs its own evolution
